dataset: Wikipedia ego network: Frank Lloyd Wright

ego.name: Frank Lloyd Wright
ego.summary: Frank Lloyd Wright was an American architect, designer, writer, and educator. He developed Prairie School and Usonian designs, advanced organic architecture, designed works including Fallingwater and the Imperial Hotel, and trained apprentices through the Taliesin Fellowship.

connections.relationship_description: Wright's mother was a teacher from the Lloyd Jones family. She encouraged his architectural ambitions from childhood and bought the Spring Green land where he built Taliesin.
connections.notes: She decorated his nursery with cathedral engravings and introduced him to Froebel Gifts.

connections.relationship_description: Wright's first wife, known as Kitty, was the mother of his children. Their marriage broke down after Wright left her for Mamah Borthwick in 1909, and their divorce was finalized in 1922.
connections.notes: Her refusal to grant an early divorce contributed to the public scandal surrounding Wright and Borthwick.

connections.relationship_description: Borthwick was Wright's partner from 1909 until her murder in 1914. They traveled in Europe, lived together at Taliesin after leaving their spouses, and helped introduce Ellen Key's feminist writing to American audiences.
connections.notes: Wright built Taliesin in part as a home and refuge for their relationship.

connections.relationship_description: Olgivanna met Wright in Chicago in November 1924, became his partner shortly afterward, and married him in 1928. They jointly established the Taliesin Fellowship in 1932 and remained married until his death.
connections.notes: After Wright's death, she became president of the Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation and continued directing the Taliesin Fellowship.

connections.relationship_description: Sullivan employed Wright at Adler & Sullivan from 1887 to 1893 and gave him substantial design responsibility. He was Wright's formative professional mentor.
connections.notes: Their relationship broke when Sullivan discovered Wright's prohibited independent residential commissions, though they later renewed contact.

connections.relationship_description: Corwin was Wright's older colleague in Silsbee's office, took the young draftsman under his wing, and became a close friend. He later shared office space with Wright after Wright opened his own Chicago practice.
connections.notes: Corwin signed several of Wright's unauthorized early residential commissions.

connections.relationship_description: Mahony joined Wright's drafting team in 1895 and created presentation drawings and watercolor renderings for his projects, including a major share of the drawings associated with the Wasmuth Portfolio.
connections.notes: She also designed furniture, leaded glass, and light fixtures for Wright houses, though her contributions were often undercredited.

connections.relationship_description: Sculptor Richard Bock met Wright through Louis Sullivan's office and collaborated with him for more than two decades on architectural sculpture, beginning with the Heller House frieze in 1896.
connections.notes: Their families socialized, and Wright designed Bock's River Forest sculpture studio, The Gnomes.

connections.relationship_description: Kaufmann commissioned Wright to design Fallingwater in 1935 for his family's Bear Run property in Pennsylvania and also commissioned the modernization of executive offices at his Pittsburgh department store.
connections.notes: Kaufmann also commissioned Wright to modernize executive offices at his Pittsburgh department store.

connections.relationship_description: Wright's father was a musician, speaker, and occasional Baptist and Unitarian preacher. His parents divorced in 1885, after which Wright said he never saw his father again.
connections.notes: William shared his love of music with his children, despite being described as a distant parent.

connections.relationship_description: Noel was Wright's second wife; their tempestuous marriage lasted from 1923 to 1927.
connections.notes: Her refusal to divorce Wright initially complicated his subsequent relationship with Olgivanna Lazović.

connections.relationship_description: Wright's son became an architect and, after a period of estrangement, assisted his father with the Imperial Hotel project in Japan and supervised work in Chicago and Tokyo.
connections.notes: Their relationship was repeatedly strained, including by disagreements over the Imperial Hotel and John's employment.

connections.relationship_description: Silsbee hired Wright as a draftsman in Chicago in 1887 after Wright had contributed drawings and construction oversight for the Lloyd Jones family's Unity Chapel.
connections.notes: Silsbee provided Wright's first sustained architectural-office experience.

connections.relationship_description: As senior partner of Adler & Sullivan, Adler worked with Wright during his apprenticeship and sent him the deed to his Oak Park house after Wright's break with Sullivan.
connections.notes: Wright praised Adler as the American Engineer and his Big Chief.

connections.relationship_description: Elmslie joined Adler & Sullivan at Wright's request, shared an office with Wright by 1890, and remained part of the Chicago circle from which the Prairie School emerged.
connections.notes: Their professional association connected Wright's early office work to the wider Prairie School network.

connections.relationship_description: Mueller was the Adler & Sullivan office foreman with whom Wright formed a bond; Wright later engaged him in construction of public and commercial projects between 1903 and 1923.
Griffin worked in Wright's Oak Park studio from 1901 to 1906, overseeing construction on notable houses and supplying landscape plans before leaving to establish his own practice.
connections.notes: The two fell out after Wright's 1905 Japan trip and never resumed a close relationship.

connections.relationship_description: Conover taught Wright civil engineering when Wright attended the University of Wisconsin as a special student in 1886.
connections.notes: Wright left the university without earning a degree.

category_summaries.summary: Anna Lloyd Jones Wright encouraged Wright's architectural ambitions and bought the Spring Green land where he built Taliesin. His parents divorced in 1885, and he later said he never saw his father again. His relationship with Mamah Borthwick ended with her murder at Taliesin in 1914. His later marriage to Olgivanna supported the Taliesin Fellowship, while his son John joined him on the Imperial Hotel project.

Wright's Chicago office training under Joseph Lyman Silsbee, Louis Sullivan, and Dankmar Adler gave him drawing experience, design responsibility, and engineering knowledge. Collaborators including Marion Mahony Griffin, Richard Bock, and Paul Mueller helped turn his designs into drawings, ornament, and buildings. Edgar J. Kaufmann's 1935 Fallingwater commission gave Wright a major opportunity to build for the Kaufmann family at Bear Run.
